title: Mood Weather
goal: Children say how they feel using weather words, and notice that friends can have different mood weather on the same day.

steps.title: Hello
steps.heading: Feelings have weather too!
steps.cue: Gather the children so they can see the TV. Wave along when the character says hello.
lines: Today we're going to find out that feelings have weather too.
Happy is sunny. Quiet is cloudy. Sad is rainy. And angry is stormy!
What's my mood weather right now? Let's think about it together.

steps.title: My mood weather today
steps.cue: When the children hold up their cards, count each weather and tap +. Once everyone is counted, tap Confirm and the character responds.
steps.prompt: What's your mood weather right now?
lines: What's the weather like inside you right now?
Pick one card and hold it up high!
steps.on_confirm: Today our class sky has {weather_list}. [[rainy: Rainy friends, that's okay. Flowers need rain to grow.]] [[stormy: Stormy friends, thank you for telling us about your angry feelings.]] Every kind of weather is a feeling, and every feeling matters!

steps.title: Weather moves
steps.heading: Let's make weather with our bodies!
steps.cue: Start the timer and call out one weather at a time. The children act it out with their bodies. When 60 seconds are up, the character wraps it up.
lines: Now let's make the weather with our bodies!
When your teacher says a weather, you become that weather. Ready?

moves.text: Sunny: make a big circle with your arms over your head
Cloudy: wiggle your body, soft and squishy

steps.done_line: Wow, all the weather came to our class! Now let's sit back down.

steps.title: Our class story today
steps.heading: Our class sky today
steps.cue: The character reads a story made from today's numbers. Afterwards, ask: 'Which weather did our class have the most of?'
steps.template: Today the sky over {class} had {weather_list}. [[weather_lead: {weather_lead} was the biggest of all.]] Weather changes every day. What mood weather will visit tomorrow? Whatever the weather, the friends in {class} will be each other's umbrellas.

steps.title: Our Class Book
steps.cue: The TV turns into a picture book of what our class made today and reads it page by page. When it's done, tap Next.
steps.cover_line: Here is the book our class made today.

steps.title: Goodbye
steps.heading: Thank you for today!
steps.cue: When the character finishes saying goodbye, tap Finish lesson. The family page link will be ready.
lines: Thank you for showing me your mood weather today.
At home, try saying: 'My mood weather today was this!'

outro: That's all for today! Thank you, friends.

home.title: Keep it going at home
tips: Ask, 'What was your mood weather today?' Choosing from sunny, cloudy, rainy or stormy makes it easy to answer.
If your child says rainy or stormy, start with 'I see.' You can ask why later, or not at all.
Share your own mood weather too. Knowing that grown-ups' weather changes helps children feel safe.
home.note: This page shows only class totals and the class story. No individual child's choice is recorded.
